data.why: The app bundles its own example structure (data/RNA-only-PDB/1fuf.pdb, data/RNA-only-PDB-clean/1fuf_clean.pdb, data/RNA-graph-pickles/1fuf.pkl) and pretrained checkpoint (best_model.pth); it takes no uploads, so there is nothing for the browser to supply.

goals: Run CPU inference with the pretrained GCN on the 1FUF ribozyme and see how many candidate sites are flagged as Mg2+ binding sites
Compare predicted and experimental Mg2+ ion positions side by side in the two Mol* 3D viewers
Check the model's ROC AUC and the Youden's-J-optimal decision threshold used to binarize predictions
Inspect the candidate-site graph representation (nodes, edges, chemical features) that feeds the GCN
Judge whether the GCN is useful as a first-pass filter for locating metal-ion binding sites compared to crystallography

review.summary: The goal and its two phases match what the README and app say the demo is for: run the pretrained GCN on 1FUF, read the metrics, and compare predicted with experimental Mg2+ in 3D. Most cited screens show what the nodes claim. The tree never does the comparison that is the interface's point (does a predicted site land on the one real ion, and at what false-positive cost?), and it has three weakly evidenced or overclaimed nodes and one bundled feature, so it needs fixes before filing.
